# Treatment definition {#sec-treatment}

We exploit two natural experiments arising from the staggered extension and creation of protected areas during the ROS survey period.

## Marovoay / Ankarafantsika (2003) {#sec-treat-maro}

The Ankarafantsika National Park was formally extended by Decree 2002-798 on 7 August 2002, merging the former *Réserve Naturelle Intégrale* (60,500 ha, 1927) with forest reserves into a 136,500 ha national park under IUCN Category II. We set the exposure year to **2003** — the first full ROS survey year following the decree.^[Decree 2002-798 was signed on 7 August 2002. Because the ROS survey is conducted annually and we attribute any treatment effect to the first full survey year following the decree, we set the treatment year to 2003. Using 2002 instead has negligible impact on the estimated ATT.]

The Marovoay observatory comprises four *fokontany* split by the Betsiboka River — a major, permanently flowing watercourse wider than 10 metres. Crossing is possible only under certain hydrological conditions, often requiring long detours or costly boat transport; in practice, flows of people, goods, and services run along the Marovoay downstream axis rather than across the river:

| Fokontany | Bank | Straight-line distance | Effective distance | Role | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bepako | East | 5.2 km | ~5.2 km | Exposed | From 2003 |
| Madiromiongana | East | 11.7 km | ~11.7 km | Exposed | From 2003 |
| Ampijoroa | West | 3.5 km | ~18.5 km (river detour) | Donor | Never |
| Maroala | West | 5.8 km | ~20.8 km (river detour) | Donor | Never |

: Marovoay site treatment assignments. Effective distances account for the Betsiboka River crossing. {#tbl-maro-sites}

The Betsiboka River constitutes a natural treatment barrier. Although the west-bank sites are geographically close to the park as the crow flies, the river imposes a substantial access penalty, roughly tripling effective travel distance.

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-maro
#| fig-cap: "Marovoay observatory and Ankarafantsika National Park. The Betsiboka River separates west-bank fokontany (control, grey) from east-bank fokontany (exposed, orange). Water features from OpenStreetMap."
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 9

# Bounding box: show the whole of Ankarafantsika plus the fokontany
ank_bb <- st_bbox(ankarafantsika_pa)
fkt_bb <- st_bbox(maro_fkt)
maro_bbox <- st_bbox(c(
  xmin = min(ank_bb["xmin"], fkt_bb["xmin"]) - 0.08,
  ymin = min(ank_bb["ymin"], fkt_bb["ymin"]) - 0.08,
  xmax = max(ank_bb["xmax"], fkt_bb["xmax"]) + 0.08,
  ymax = max(ank_bb["ymax"], fkt_bb["ymax"]) + 0.08
), crs = 4326)

# Filter water features: Betsiboka river + water bodies within 1 km
betsiboka_named <- osm_water_maro$lines |> filter(name == "Betsiboka")
betsiboka_buf <- betsiboka_named |>
  st_transform(32738) |> st_union() |> st_buffer(1000) |> st_transform(4326)

water_lines <- tryCatch(st_crop(betsiboka_named, maro_bbox), error = function(e) NULL)
water_polys <- tryCatch({
  wp <- st_crop(osm_water_maro$polys, maro_bbox)
  wp[st_intersects(wp, betsiboka_buf, sparse = FALSE)[, 1], ]
}, error = function(e) NULL)
water_mpolys <- tryCatch({
  wm <- st_crop(osm_water_maro$mpolys, maro_bbox)
  wm[st_intersects(wm, betsiboka_buf, sparse = FALSE)[, 1], ]
}, error = function(e) NULL)

WATER_COL <- "#1976D2"
ank_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(ankarafantsika_pa)))

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ankarafantsika_pa, fill = "#A5D6A7", color = "#388E3C",
          alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.6)

if (!is.null(water_polys) && nrow(water_polys) > 0)
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = water_polys, fill = WATER_COL, color = WATER_COL,
                   linewidth = 0.1)
if (!is.null(water_mpolys) && nrow(water_mpolys) > 0)
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = water_mpolys, fill = WATER_COL, color = WATER_COL,
                   linewidth = 0.1)
if (!is.null(water_lines) && nrow(water_lines) > 0)
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = water_lines, color = WATER_COL, linewidth = 0.7)

maro_fkt_lab <- maro_fkt |>
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2],
    nudge_x = if_else(fokontany == "Maroala", -0.06, 0),
    nudge_y = if_else(fokontany == "Maroala",  0.04, 0)
  )

p +
  annotate("text", x = ank_centroid[1], y = ank_centroid[2],
           label = "Ankarafantsika\nNational Park",
           color = "#1B5E20", fontface = "bold.italic", size = 4.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = maro_fkt, aes(color = river_side, shape = river_side),
          size = 4, stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = maro_fkt_lab,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat,
        label = paste0(fokontany, "\n(", dist_km, " km)"),
        color = river_side),
    size = 3, fontface = "bold", box.padding = 0.8,
    nudge_x = maro_fkt_lab$nudge_x,
    nudge_y = maro_fkt_lab$nudge_y,
    min.segment.length = 0, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("east" = "#E65100", "west" = "#616161"),
    labels = c("east" = "East bank (exposed)", "west" = "West bank (donor)"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("east" = 17, "west" = 16),
    labels = c("east" = "East bank (exposed)", "west" = "West bank (donor)"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.25) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(maro_bbox["xmin"], maro_bbox["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(maro_bbox["ymin"], maro_bbox["ymax"])) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Historical expansion of Ankarafantsika {#sec-expansion}

Ankarafantsika was first gazetted as a *Réserve Naturelle Intégrale* (RNI) in 1927, covering approximately 60,500 ha of the central plateau. A contiguous 75,000 ha forest reserve was classified in 1929. These two early designations imposed different nominal restrictions, but critically different *de facto* situations for the east-bank *fokontany*:

- **The 1929 forest reserve** was not a nature conservation zone but a timber and resource reserve under the forest administration. Subsequent analyses found no effective enforcement over this area, and subsistence agriculture, cattle grazing, and charcoal production continued unimpeded [@brondeau1999]. The forest reserve regime imposed no binding constraint on adjacent communities.

- **The 1927 RNI** was geographically separate from the communities of Bepako and Madiromiongana: the RNI covered the inland plateau to the north-east, while these villages border the forest reserve zone to the south and west of the plateau. The east-bank *fokontany* therefore had no direct interface with the strictly protected RNI.

In 2002, the RNI, the forest reserves, and the Ampijoroa Forestry Station were merged into a single national park (Decree 2002-798, ~130,000 ha), later adjusted to 136,513 ha in 2015 (Decree 2015-730). @fig-expansion, reproduced from @alonso2002, illustrates the spatial extent of the 2002 consolidation.

![Spatial extent of the 2002 Ankarafantsika expansion, from the original RNI (dark green) to the national park (light green). Source: @alonso2002.](media/Alonso_Shuldenberg_2002.png){#fig-expansion width=80%}

The 2002 reclassification was therefore the **first event to impose binding land-use restrictions** on the east-bank communities: slash-and-burn agriculture (*tavy*), charcoal production, and non-timber forest product extraction within the newly unified park were explicitly prohibited and — crucially — enforced. Enforcement capacity was supported by international conservation funding from the World Bank and bilateral donors as part of Madagascar's third Environmental Action Plan. The transition from a nominally protected but effectively open-access forest reserve to a strictly patrolled national park constitutes our treatment event.

### PA interaction patterns (2025 resurvey) {#sec-maro-usage}

The 2025 resurvey included a dedicated module on protected area usage (UM), asking all households whether they visit the PA zone, what activities they pursue there, and — for non-visitors — why they do not go. These responses help characterise the behavioural asymmetry across the Betsiboka.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-maro-usage
#| tbl-cap: "PA interaction at Marovoay by fokontany (2025 resurvey). 'Visit PA zone' = any visit, including leisure. 'Extractive use' = food gathering, woodcutting, cultivation, grazing, or craft materials. '% cite forbidden' = share of non-visitors citing legal prohibition."

res_deb_25 <- haven::read_dta("data/ROS_MDG_microdata/2025/res_deb.dta") |>
  mutate(
    j5 = as.character(j5),
    Observatory = case_when(
      as.character(j0) == "3"  ~ "Marovoay",
      as.character(j0) == "21" ~ "Alaotra"
    ),
    Site = case_when(
      j0 == 3 & str_detect(str_to_lower(j4), "^bepako")          ~ "Bepako",
      j0 == 3 & str_detect(str_to_lower(j4), "^madiromiongana")  ~ "Madiromiongana",
      j0 == 3 & str_detect(str_to_lower(j4), "^ampijoroa")       ~ "Ampijoroa",
      j0 == 3 & str_detect(str_to_lower(j4), "^maroala")         ~ "Maroala",
      j0 == 21 ~ j4
    ),
    bank = case_when(
      Site %in% c("Bepako", "Madiromiongana") ~ "East",
      Site %in% c("Ampijoroa", "Maroala")     ~ "West"
    )
  )

um1_25 <- haven::read_dta("data/ROS_MDG_microdata/2025/res_um1.dta") |>
  mutate(j5 = as.character(j5)) |>
  inner_join(res_deb_25 |> select(j5, Observatory, Site, bank), by = "j5")

um2_25 <- haven::read_dta("data/ROS_MDG_microdata/2025/res_um2.dta") |>
  mutate(j5 = as.character(j5)) |>
  inner_join(res_deb_25 |> select(j5, Observatory, Site, bank), by = "j5")

# Households with any extractive use (um2_lig 1-8)
extractive_hh <- um2_25 |>
  filter(um2_a == 1, um2_lig %in% 1:8) |>
  distinct(j5) |>
  mutate(extractive = TRUE)

res_deb_25 |>
  filter(Observatory == "Marovoay") |>
  left_join(um1_25 |> select(j5, um1, um1d_a), by = "j5") |>
  left_join(extractive_hh, by = "j5") |>
  mutate(extractive = replace_na(extractive, FALSE)) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `% visit PA zone` = round(sum(um1 == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / n() * 100, 0),
    `% extractive use` = round(sum(extractive) / n() * 100, 0),
    `% cite 'forbidden'` = round(
      sum(um1d_a == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(um1 == 2, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 0
    ),
    .by = c(Site, bank)
  ) |>
  arrange(match(Site, c("Bepako", "Madiromiongana", "Ampijoroa", "Maroala"))) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(bank = "Bank") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "PA Interaction by Fokontany",
    subtitle = "Marovoay observatory, 2025 resurvey (N = 519 households)"
  )
```

The visitation asymmetry is clear — 38% of east-bank households report visiting the park zone, versus 15% on the west bank — but the nature of these visits requires qualification. Among visitors on both banks, the dominant reported activity is *promenade/loisir* (leisure walks), cited by 67% of users. Only 10% of east-bank households report any extractive use of the park (food gathering, woodcutting), and 91% of all visitors go only a few times per year.

The more informative signal comes from non-visitors. At Madiromiongana — the east-bank fokontany closest to the park's core — 34% of non-visitors cite legal prohibition as their reason for not going, compared to 2% at Maroala on the west bank. Across both banks, the dominant reason for non-use is distance (*lavitra*), cited in free-text responses by 54% of Marovoay non-visitors. This pattern is consistent with the treatment design: the river barrier makes the park *behaviourally distant* for west-bank communities even where it is *geographically close*, while east-bank communities are aware of and constrained by the park's legal status.

## Alaotra / Lac Alaotra (2008) {#sec-treat-ala}

Lac Alaotra is Madagascar's largest lake and a critical habitat for the Alaotran gentle lemur (*Hapalemur alaotrensis*). The Ramsar Convention listed the site in 2003. In 2015, the lake and its marshlands were formally designated as a *Paysage Harmonieux Protégé* (PHP, 425 km², IUCN Category V), though enforcement through community-based natural resource management (CBNRM) agreements and *transferts de gestion* had intensified from around 2008 under the management of Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust. A temporary protection decree (*Arrêté* 381/2007, 1 August 2007) preceded the intensification. We set the exposure year to **2008** to remain consistent with the annual-survey convention applied to Ankarafantsika (attributing effects to the first full survey year following the operative decree).^[An alternative treatment year of 2007 is defensible; using 2007 instead has negligible impact on the estimated ATT, given that the post-treatment window contains up to seven observations under either assumption.]

The observatory's seven *fokontany* (across three historical survey sites) all depend on the lake-marsh ecosystem. Unlike Ankarafantsika, there is no natural barrier separating "exposed" from "unexposed" communities. All communities interact with the PA. A complication specific to Alaotra is the proximity of some eastern hamlets to two additional protected areas: the **Corridor Ankeniheny-Zahamena** (CAZ, IUCN Category VI, managed by Conservation International) and the **Zahamena National Park** (IUCN Category II), which lies north of the CAZ. The hamlet of Mangabe lies closer to the CAZ boundary (~14 km) than to the Lac Alaotra PHP, creating dual-PA exposure.

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-ala
#| fig-cap: "Alaotra observatory and surrounding protected areas. Lac Alaotra PHP (green), Corridor Ankeniheny-Zahamena (CAZ, orange), Zahamena National Park (light orange). Fokontany centroids from 2025 GPS survey; distances to nearest PA boundary."
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8

ala_bbox <- st_bbox(c(xmin = 48.00, ymin = -18.10, xmax = 48.80, ymax = -17.20),
                    crs = 4326)

ala_clip <- tryCatch(st_crop(alaotra_pa, ala_bbox), error = function(e) NULL)
caz_clip <- tryCatch(st_crop(caz_pa, ala_bbox), error = function(e) NULL)
zah_clip <- tryCatch(st_crop(zahamena_pa, ala_bbox), error = function(e) NULL)

p <- ggplot()

# PA polygons
if (!is.null(ala_clip) && nrow(ala_clip) > 0) {
  ala_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(ala_clip)))
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = ala_clip, fill = "#A5D6A7", color = "#388E3C",
                   alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.6) +
    annotate("text", x = ala_centroid[1], y = ala_centroid[2],
             label = "Lac Alaotra\nPHP", color = "#1B5E20",
             fontface = "bold.italic", size = 3.5, alpha = 0.8)
}
if (!is.null(caz_clip) && nrow(caz_clip) > 0) {
  caz_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(caz_clip)))
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = caz_clip, fill = "#FFE0B2", color = "#E65100",
                   alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.6) +
    annotate("text", x = caz_centroid[1], y = caz_centroid[2],
             label = "Corridor\nAnkeniheny-\nZahamena",
             color = "#BF360C", fontface = "bold.italic", size = 3, alpha = 0.8)
}
if (!is.null(zah_clip) && nrow(zah_clip) > 0) {
  zah_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(zah_clip)))
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = zah_clip, fill = "#FFCCBC", color = "#BF360C",
                   alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.5) +
    annotate("text", x = zah_centroid[1], y = zah_centroid[2],
             label = "Zahamena\nNational Park",
             color = "#BF360C", fontface = "bold.italic", size = 3, alpha = 0.8)
}

# Fokontany points
p +
  geom_sf(data = ala_fkt, aes(shape = nearest_pa), size = 3,
          color = "#1B5E20", stroke = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = ala_fkt |> mutate(lon = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
                             lat = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]),
    aes(x = lon, y = lat,
        label = paste0(fokontany, " (", round(pmin(dist_php, dist_caz), 1), " km)")),
    size = 2.5, fontface = "bold", box.padding = 0.6,
    min.segment.length = 0
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Lac Alaotra PHP" = 16, "Corridor Ankeniheny-Zahamena" = 17),
    name = "Nearest PA"
  ) +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.25) +
  labs(
    subtitle = "All fokontany exposed at observatory level from 2008 (CBNRM enforcement)"
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(ala_bbox["xmin"], ala_bbox["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(ala_bbox["ymin"], ala_bbox["ymax"])) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### PA interaction patterns (2025 resurvey) {#sec-ala-usage}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ala-usage
#| tbl-cap: "PA interaction at Alaotra by fokontany (2025 resurvey). 'Visit PA zone' includes any visit to the lake-marsh area. 'Extractive use' = food gathering, fishing/hunting, cultivation, grazing, or woodcutting within the zone. Fishing/hunting shown separately as it dominates extractive use."

res_deb_25 |>
  filter(Observatory == "Alaotra") |>
  left_join(um1_25 |> select(j5, um1), by = "j5") |>
  left_join(extractive_hh, by = "j5") |>
  left_join(
    um2_25 |> filter(um2_a == 1, um2_lig == 4) |>
      distinct(j5) |> mutate(fishes = TRUE),
    by = "j5"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    extractive = replace_na(extractive, FALSE),
    fishes = replace_na(fishes, FALSE)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `% visit zone` = round(sum(um1 == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / n() * 100, 0),
    `% extractive` = round(sum(extractive) / n() * 100, 0),
    `% fish/hunt` = round(sum(fishes) / n() * 100, 0),
    .by = Site
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(`% extractive`)) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "PA Interaction by Fokontany",
    subtitle = "Alaotra observatory, 2025 resurvey (N = 507 households)"
  )
```

While 37–54% of households report visiting the lake-marsh zone, this headline rate is misleading as a measure of PA dependence. The survey question (*"Vous arrive-t-il d'aller dans la zone?"*) captures any visit, and the majority of visitors report non-extractive purposes — leisure walks, unspecified *other* reasons, or ritual activities. Among those who do visit, 78% go only a few times per year.

Extractive use is far less prevalent and far less uniform across sites. Fishing and hunting (the dominant extractive activity, reflecting traditional lake use) involves 21% of households in Ambatomanga but none in Avaradrano or Feramanga Atsimo. The overall extractive rate across the observatory is 13% of all households. The relatively uniform *visiting* rate but sharply differentiated *extractive* rate suggests that proximity to the lake-marsh ecosystem — rather than engagement with PA-regulated resources — drives the visiting pattern.

We therefore treat the **entire observatory as a single treated unit**, aggregated to a site-level mean. The uniform exposure assumption is stronger for the CBNRM enforcement mechanism (which applies to all lake-adjacent communities) than for individual extractive dependence (which varies).

### Visit frequency across both observatories

@fig-visit-freq summarises the intensity of PA zone visitation across all survey sites. The white segment — households who never visit — dominates most sites, particularly in Marovoay where the river barrier limits access. Among those who do visit, the overwhelming majority go only a few times per year (grey). Regular visitors (monthly or more, shown in warm colours) are a thin sliver confined to the closest sites: Bepako on the east bank of Ankarafantsika, and Ambohidrony at Alaotra.

```{r}
#| label: fig-visit-freq
#| fig-cap: "PA zone visit frequency by site (2025 resurvey). Each bar represents 100% of households in a site. White = does not visit; grey = few times per year; warm colours = monthly or more. Sites ordered by total share of visitors."
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 9

# --- Site assignment ---
hh_site_fig <- res_deb_25 |>
  mutate(
    site = case_when(
      Observatory == "Marovoay" & str_detect(j4, "(?i)bepako|bepàko")     ~ "Bepako",
      Observatory == "Marovoay" & str_detect(j4, "(?i)madiro")             ~ "Madiromiongana",
      Observatory == "Marovoay" & str_detect(j4, "(?i)ampijoroa|ampijoro") ~ "Ampijoroa",
      Observatory == "Marovoay" & str_detect(j4, "(?i)maroala|maroàla")    ~ "Maroala",
      TRUE ~ j4
    )
  )

# --- Max visit frequency per household ---
hh_freq_fig <- um2_25 |>
  filter(um2_a == 1, !is.na(um2_b)) |>
  summarise(freq_max = max(um2_b), .by = j5)

# --- Classify each household ---
visit_data <- hh_site_fig |>
  left_join(um1_25 |> select(j5, um1), by = "j5") |>
  left_join(hh_freq_fig, by = "j5") |>
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      um1 == 2 | is.na(um1) ~ "Does not visit",
      is.na(freq_max)       ~ "Does not visit",
      freq_max == 1 ~ "Few times/year",
      freq_max == 2 ~ "Few times/month",
      freq_max == 3 ~ "Once/week",
      freq_max == 4 ~ "Several times/week"
    ),
    category = factor(category, levels = c(
      "Does not visit", "Few times/year", "Few times/month",
      "Once/week", "Several times/week"
    ))
  )

# --- Percentages by site ---
site_freq_fig <- visit_data |>
  count(Observatory, site, category) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100, .by = c(Observatory, site))

# --- Order by total % who visit (most on top) ---
visit_order <- site_freq_fig |>
  filter(category != "Does not visit") |>
  summarise(pct_visit = sum(pct), .by = site) |>
  arrange(pct_visit)

site_freq_fig <- site_freq_fig |>
  mutate(site = factor(site, levels = visit_order$site))

# --- Plot ---
ggplot(site_freq_fig, aes(x = pct, y = site, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.7, color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Does not visit"       = "white",
      "Few times/year"       = "#B0BEC5",
      "Few times/month"      = "#FFB74D",
      "Once/week"            = "#FF7043",
      "Several times/week"   = "#D32F2F"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Observatory, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "% of all households",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )
```

## Extensions (2006–2007) {#sec-treat-ext}

Three additional observatory–PA pairs provide shorter exposure windows (see [Chapter 5](05_extensions.qmd)):

- **Farafangana / CFAV** (IUCN VI, 2006) — Corridor Forestier Ambositra-Vondrozo
- **Toliara North / Amoron'i Onilahy** (IUCN VI, 2007)
- **Fénérive East / Tampolo** (IUCN IV, 2007) — coastal forest reserve

# Outcome variable and panel construction {#sec-outcome}

## Equivalised income

Total household income (`revtot`) is adjusted for household composition using the **OECD-modified equivalence scale**:

$$
\text{equiv} = 1 + 0.5 \times (\text{additional adults}) + 0.3 \times (\text{children under 14})
$$

computed from individual-level demographic data in the ROS survey. The resulting equivalised income is winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles within each year to limit the influence of extreme observations. The primary outcome is **log equivalised income**.

## Village-level aggregation {#sec-aggregation}

The ROS operates as a **rotating panel**: each observatory tracks a fixed set of households, but approximately 15% of households leave the sample each year (through death, migration, or attrition), with replacement by newly sampled households following the original random sampling design. Over a 10-year horizon, cumulative attrition reaches roughly 80% of the initial cohort [@ChabeFerret2024]. Attrition is non-random: traceable attritors disproportionately include migrants whose departure is itself potentially income-related, which would violate the balanced-panel assumptions underlying individual-level panel estimators.

We therefore analyse the data at the **village (*fokontany*) level**, aggregating household-level income to village-year medians. This choice is justified on two grounds. First, the rotating design with random replacement preserves cross-sectional representativeness at each wave: village-year statistics consistently estimate the same population quantity across years, even as the composition of surveyed households changes. Second, gsynth requires a balanced unit-by-year panel matrix and is designed for unit-level (here village-level) variation; household-level estimation with an interactive FE model would require substantially more pre-treatment periods to identify individual-level factor loadings.

# Donor pool selection {#sec-donor-pool}

The generalized synthetic control method requires that donor units be **unexposed to treatment**. We start with 9 donor observatories (Antsirabe, Antsohihy, Tsiroanomandidy, Farafangana, Ambovombe, Toliara North, Fénérive East, Mahanoro, Itasy), providing approximately 60 donor sites.

A systematic spatial audit ([Appendix B](A2_donor_validity.qmd)) checks whether these donors are themselves adjacent to active PAs during the study period. Using a dynamic WDPA layer that records when each PA became legally operative, we flag any donor commune within 20 km of an active PA boundary as **also exposed**.

| Status | Observatories | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Clean** | Antsirabe (02), Tsiroanomandidy (13), Ambovombe (16), Mahanoro (25), Itasy (41) | No active PA within 20 km during 1999–2014 |
| **Also exposed** | Antsohihy (12), Farafangana (15), Toliara North (23), Fénérive East (24) | PA created within 20 km during study period |

: Donor pool PA exposure classification. {#tbl-donor-status}

The main results use the full 9-donor pool; robustness checks ([Appendix C](A3_robustness.qmd)) confirm that restricting to the 5 clean donors does not materially change the estimates. In the extension analysis ([Chapter 5](05_extensions.qmd)), the also-exposed donors become *treated* units with their own PA exposure — a design feature rather than a threat.

# Generalized synthetic control {#sec-gsynth}

We use the generalized synthetic control method (gsynth) of @Xu2017 to estimate treatment effects. For each treated unit $i$ in post-treatment period $t$, gsynth models the outcome as:

$$
Y_{it} = \alpha_i + \xi_t + \boldsymbol{\lambda}_i' \boldsymbol{f}_t + D_{it} \cdot \delta_{it} + \varepsilon_{it}
$$

where $\alpha_i$ are unit fixed effects, $\xi_t$ are time fixed effects, $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_i$ are unit-specific factor loadings, $\boldsymbol{f}_t$ are common time factors, and $D_{it}$ is the exposure indicator. The interactive fixed effects ($\boldsymbol{\lambda}_i' \boldsymbol{f}_t$) relax the parallel trends assumption by allowing units to follow heterogeneous time paths driven by unobserved factors.

Key implementation choices:

- **Unit of analysis** — site-level (*fokontany*) medians of log equivalised income (see @sec-outcome).
- **Factor selection** — leave-one-out cross-validation over $r \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$.
- **Inference** — parametric bootstrap with 200 replications.
- **Minimum pre-treatment periods** — $\text{min.T0} = 3$ to ensure adequate pre-treatment fit.

We estimate **two separate models**, reflecting the distinct nature of each treatment:

1. **Marovoay model**: Treated units = Madiromiongana and Bepako (east bank, from 2003). Donors = all other rural observatory sites, including the Marovoay west-bank sites (Ampijoroa, Maroala). With 2 treated sites, gsynth estimates unit-specific counterfactuals.

2. **Alaotra model**: Treated unit = aggregated Alaotra observatory "ALA" (from 2008). Donors = all non-Alaotra rural observatory sites, including all four Marovoay *fokontany*. With a single treated unit, this reduces to interactive FE synthetic control.

## Inference with few treated units {#sec-inference}

A fundamental constraint of this design is the small number of treated units: 2 sites for Marovoay, 1 for Alaotra. With so few treated clusters, asymptotic inference is unreliable regardless of the estimator chosen. The parametric bootstrap standard errors from gsynth are correspondingly wide.

An exact permutation bound is informative. For Marovoay, the set of observable units within the observatory comprises 4 sites (2 east-bank, 2 west-bank). The number of ways to assign exactly 2 of these 4 units as "exposed" is $\binom{4}{2} = 6$. Under Fisher's sharp null, the **minimum achievable p-value** is therefore $1/6 \approx 0.167$ for a one-sided test. No test based solely on these 4 sites can produce a p-value below 0.167 for the one-sided hypothesis, regardless of the observed effect magnitude. When the three Alaotra sites are included as additional control donors in a long-run DiD (thereby expanding the donor pool for permutation), the allocation count rises to $\binom{7}{2} = 21$ and the minimum achievable p-value falls to $1/21 \approx 0.048$.

We report gsynth bootstrap confidence intervals and p-values throughout but interpret them in light of this power ceiling. The inability to reject the null at conventional thresholds does not imply absence of effect; it reflects the inherent inferential limitations of quasi-experimental designs with a handful of geographic units. Placebo-in-space tests ([Appendix C](A3_robustness.qmd)) provide complementary evidence on the uniqueness of estimated effects.

# Towards household-level DiD {#sec-did-roadmap}

The gsynth approach is well-suited to the current data but has an important limitation: it operates at the site level, discarding within-site household heterogeneity. A household-level DiD is not feasible with the current rotating-panel design: approximately 80% of households are replaced between survey waves, making panel-based estimation unreliable. The 2026 survey wave will enable a richer design:

- **Callaway–Sant'Anna DiD** at the household level, exploiting four staggered treatment cohorts (Ankarafantsika 2003, Farafangana/Toliara/Fénérive 2006–07, Alaotra 2008, plus never-treated).
- **Not-yet-treated controls** — Alaotra households observed in 2003–2007 (before their own treatment) serve as additional controls for the Ankarafantsika cohort.
- **Household covariates** for conditional parallel trends (demographics, pre-treatment income, agricultural dependence).
- **Sun–Abraham event studies** via `fixest::sunab()` as a complementary estimator.

This forward-looking design is discussed further in [Chapter 6](06_discussion.qmd).
